title: Lesson 9: Focused Read-aloud, Session 2: Does the Sun Sleep? Noticing Sun, Moon, and Star Patterns
objective: Students will learn to distinguish information from illustrations and text about star patterns and record observations about the sky using writing and discussion.

what_is_taught.skill: distinguish information learned from illustrations versus text
describe patterns of stars using information from text and illustrations
use prepositions to understand spatial relationships in a poem
move physical signs to represent prepositions in a poem
participate in partner discussions to explain concepts
use vocabulary words related to stars and constellations
record observations in writing about the sky
use sentence frames to support writing
engage in shared writing to describe nighttime activities
use word walls and anchor charts to support vocabulary and spelling
observe and describe a scientific demonstration about light
watch and interpret a time-lapse video of stars

student_actions.oral_production: participate in partner and group discussions to explain and describe observations and concepts
student_actions.written_production: write observations and descriptions in a notebook and shared writing form
student_actions.procedural_application: apply knowledge of prepositions by moving signs to correct spatial locations
student_actions.investigation_handson: observe a scientific demonstration and a video to investigate star visibility and light
student_actions.representation_modeling: use physical signs to represent sun, moon, and stars and their positions
student_actions.reasoning_explanation: explain why stars are not visible during the day using evidence from text, video, and demonstration
student_actions.comprehension_response: answer questions about text and illustrations to describe star patterns and nighttime activities in writing and discussion, including using sentence frames and charts to support responses and writing guidance, and participate in shared writing activities to describe nighttime activities using vocabulary and word walls, and discuss observations from video and demonstration about stars and light visibility in the sky

teacher_actions.direct_instruction: Model reading the poem and informational text fluently; demonstrate use of prepositions with signs; model use of word walls and anchor charts to support vocabulary and writing; demonstrate scientific concepts with flashlight and video; model writing and spelling strategies.
prompts_that_cue_student_response: What information are we learning about stars from this sentence?
Why can't we see stars during the day?
What new information can we learn from the illustration on this page?
Based on the information from both the text and the illustrations, what is a constellation?
What is one piece of new information you have learned about patterns of the stars?
What did you notice about the stars in the night sky?
How would you describe the light from the star (flashlight)?
Did the light from the star (flashlight) change? What caused it to seem dimmer or harder to see?
Why can't we see stars during the day?
What are people doing when the moon is out?

scope.breadth: multiple related texts and media about stars, sun, moon, and night sky
scope.depth: focus on distinguishing information from text and illustrations and recording observations

context.stimulus_provided: text, illustrations, video, scientific demonstration, poem, anchor charts, word walls

sections_covered.warm_up: Poem and Movement: 'Where Are They? The Sun, Moon, and Stars' Poem
sections_covered.direct_instruction: Focused Read-aloud: Does the Sun Sleep?: Noticing Sun, Moon, and Star Patterns, Pages 16-21
sections_covered.guided_practice: Engaging the Scientist: 'Why Can't We See Stars during the Day?'
sections_covered.check_for_understanding: Shared Writing: Describing What People Do at Night

supports.english_language_learners: Includes vocabulary translation practice, sentence frames, and multiple exposures to video and text to support ELLs.
supports.universal_design_udl: Uses multiple modalities including movement, visuals, partner talk, and writing supports.
supports.below_level_reinforce: Teacher models and provides sentence frames and guided writing support.
supports.above_level_extend: Encourages students to use home language translations and self- and peer-correction during vocabulary practice.

assessment.method: Observation of student participation in discussions, movement activity, writing in Sky notebook, and shared writing.
assessment.recognition_vs_production: Both recognition of vocabulary and concepts and production of oral and written responses.

notes: The lesson integrates comprehension of informational text with vocabulary development, scientific observation, and writing. It includes supports for English language learners and emphasizes respectful behavior during movement activities.

text_complexity.quantitative: Read-aloud text pages 16-21; quantitative measure not specified due to read-aloud mediation
text_complexity.qualitative: Informational text with illustrations; moderate language and knowledge demands related to astronomy concepts
text_complexity.reader_and_task: Students listen to read-aloud, observe illustrations and video, participate in discussions, and write observations with scaffolding.
